newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-JUDGING SYSTEM COULD CHANGE.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-JUDGING SYSTEM COULD CHANGE.

text.p: International Skating Union (ISU) president Ottavio Cinquanta said on Tuesday that changes to figure skating's esoteric judging system could occur before next year's Winter Olympics in Japan.
Cinquanta said that amendments to existing rules could take place "if we can make them within the framework of the present regulations".
But he stressed that major changes could only be passed by the bienniel ISU congress, which does not meet until mid-1998.
Cinquanta is known to be upset at the confusing result of the men's event at the European championships in Paris in January, which he felt was incomprehensible to the public.
He has already ordered an immediate review of the placing system which determines results in figure skating, with a committee to study alternatives and report back to the ISU Council meeting in June.
Cinquanta is backed in his desire to set up a more easily understood system by International Olympic Committee president Juan Antonio Samaranch.
"We ask only one thing -- that the public understand clearly what is going on on the ice," Samaranch said.
In Paris, with final skater Andrei Vlascenko of Germany still to perform, the order was Viacheslav Zagorodniuk first, followed by Alexei Urmanov, Ilya Kulik and Philippe Candeloro.
After Vlascenko skated, the order switched to put Urmanov on top, Candeloro second, Zagorodniuk third and Kulik fourth. Vlascenko took sixth place.
Cinquanta had said earlier that just because millions did not understand that result "it does not mean the system is wrong".
"But it does mean the ISU must do something to ensure the spectators are not in that position again," he said.
